rows.title: A year after 'Liberation Day,' Trump's tariffs are hurting small businesses
rows.standfirst: Many small-business owners say the uncertainty that goes along with the high cost of the Trump administration's emergency tariffs is driving away customers and eating into profits.

rows.title: Drive slower, go electric, don't drive at all? Americans weigh options for saving gas
rows.standfirst: With gasoline prices averaging above $4 a gallon nationally, drivers are grappling with a sharp rise in fuel costs. Here are some ideas to consider if you're trying to cut your fuel costs.

rows.title: How Bill Phillips used flowing water to model the economy
rows.standfirst: Bill Phillips was an outsider to economics, but he used a machine and a chart to change the way we think about the government's role in a capitalist economy.

rows.title: Beer cans, helium balloons and mortgages: An unexpected mix of things affected by war
rows.standfirst: It's not just oil and gas that are affected by the Iran war. All sorts of shortages and price spikes are starting to pop up that stand to affect people's daily lives.

rows.title: Why infinite scroll's inventor wants to kill his creation
rows.standfirst: We practically live on our phones these days. Scrolling and scrolling, endlessly. Entrepreneur Aza Raskin is responsible for creating this infinite scroll. He also testified against Meta, who have been under fire — and in court — charged with making their apps addictive to children.

rows.title: Is the economy red, orange, yellow or green?
rows.standfirst: Come see Planet Money live on stage! 12 cities. Details and tix here: planetmoneybook.com

rows.title: Questions to help you get 'financially naked' with your partner
rows.standfirst: Having "brutally honest conversations" about money can bring couples closer together, says Vivian Tu, a financial educator. She shares questions to ask your partner at every relationship stage.

rows.title: When legal sports betting surges, so do Americans' financial problems
rows.standfirst: As online betting has grown in popularity, a new report from the New York Federal Reserve builds on the troubling link between legal sports wagering and financial health.

rows.title: Tax refunds are trending a bit higher this year. Here's how people are spending them
rows.standfirst: Some people are splurging. Others are finding that their refunds are being swallowed up by the rising cost of gas.

rows.title: Reese’s heir vs. chocolate skimpflation
rows.standfirst: Live event info and tickets here.

rows.title: Jobs that new college grads are (and are not) landing
rows.standfirst: Come see Planet Money live on stage! 12 cities. Details and tix here: planetmoneybook.com

rows.title: The labor market springs back to life in March as employers add 178,000 jobs
rows.standfirst: The U.S. job market perked up last month as employers added 178,000 jobs. The unemployment rate dipped to 4.3%, mainly because the number of people seeking work declined.

rows.title: Verdicts against Meta and Google may bring a new era of big tech accountability
rows.standfirst: Advocates hope recent verdicts against social media platforms will build momentum for bigger changes in Silicon Valley.

rows.title: What's next for Meta in the wake of trial losses and layoffs?
rows.standfirst: The company behind Facebook and Instagram has lost two major court cases and appears to be scaling back on the virtual reality Metaverse.

rows.title: Trump administration sues three states over attempts to regulate prediction markets
rows.standfirst: The suits are the most ambitious effort to date that the Trump administration has gone to try to override state laws and set the rules for the fast-growing and increasingly divisive betting industry.

rows.title: How to get through the Strait of Hormuz
rows.standfirst: The United States has been at war with Iran since February 28th. And for a month and a half, Iran’s main leverage over the U.S. has been their control over the Strait of Hormuz — a key global shipping route. Iran has attacked ships that try to pass without approval. And recently they’ve insinuated that one part of the Strait — the part near Oman — is not safe. Which means that captains had to go right by Iran’s shores to get through the Strait … effectively creating a chokepoint for the global economy.

rows.title: Why Hollywood heavyweights oppose the Paramount and Warner Brothers deal
rows.standfirst: Two entertainment and media powerhouses are likely to become one. So why aren’t the artists happy about it?

rows.title: Fuel protests have Ireland's government facing possible no-confidence vote
rows.standfirst: The prime minister announced new tax cuts to try to end the crisis that began after the U.S.-Israel war on Iran led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The government could face a no-confidence vote over its response to the fuel protests.

rows.title: The labor economics of 'Alien' — and its lessons for inequality on Earth
rows.standfirst: Behind the acid blood and jump scares of the Alien franchise is an even more insidious horror: a single employer with unchecked power. How Weyland-Yutani helps explain monopsony — and the rise of inequality on Earth.

rows.title: 2 local TV giants merged. Then a court stepped in
rows.standfirst: Local TV giant Nexstar's $6.2 billion deal to acquire rival Tegna won speedy approval from Trump administration regulators. But it faces a tough challenge from a pair of antitrust lawsuits.

rows.title: How the workplace helps you win Survivor
rows.standfirst: With the 50th season of Survivor underway, three former Survivor winners tell us how some of the skills they learned in their careers helped them win the show.

rows.title: You might be suffering from AI brain fry
rows.standfirst: Is AI in the workplace lightening your load...or frying your brain?

rows.title: Can you really do what you love?
rows.standfirst: They say do what you love and you’ll never work a day in your life. But c’mon. Is that possible in this day and age? On today’s show, we speak to a tech investor who tells us the ingredients he believes are needed to make passion pay. And we hear from an economist who’s run the numbers on luck.

rows.title: Love corporate jargon? You might be worse at your job (CT+)
rows.standfirst: Leverage. Bandwidth. Circle back.

rows.title: How AI is getting better at finding security holes
rows.standfirst: Anthropic announced this week that its new model found security flaws in "every major operating system and web browser." Even before the news, AI models had gotten dramatically better at finding bugs.

rows.title: BOOKstore Economics
rows.standfirst: How do bookstores choose the books they stock, and how does that affect what customers read? It may not seem like it, but every shelf in a bookstore is a highly valuable and contested piece of commercial real estate. And for every new book that a bookstore decides to stock, there are thousands of others that did not make the cut. So how do bookstores make those decisions? And how will the Planet Money book fare under the discerning eyes of the booksellers, the final gatekeepers in the long gauntlet of the publishing industry?

rows.title: Inflation surges to highest level in nearly 2 years as energy costs spike
rows.standfirst: Consumer prices in March were up 3.3% from a year ago, the biggest annual increase in nearly two years. Higher gasoline prices tied to the war with Iran accounted for much of the surge.

rows.title: Women are getting most of the new jobs. What's going on with men?
rows.standfirst: Over the past year, the vast majority of new jobs have gone to women. One economist says to help men find work, we need to embrace ways to "make girly jobs appeal to manly men."

rows.title: How governments have tried to hide information about the Iran war online
rows.standfirst: Governments are blocking the internet, banning social media posts and cutting access to commercial satellite images. But experts say that efforts to censor information have had mixed results.

rows.title: Well-timed bets on Polymarket tied to the Iran war draw calls for investigations from lawmakers
rows.standfirst: Calls are increasing inside Congress for investigations into the prediction market platform Polymarket after the latest instance where groups of anonymous traders made strategic, well-timed bets on a major geopolitical event hours before it occurred.

rows.title: The hidden power keeping wages low
rows.standfirst: For decades, economists gave short shrift to the idea of monopsony — a power employers can have to suppress wages. Now a wave of research suggests it's everywhere, and a new book argues it's key to understanding today's inequality.

rows.title: Here are 3 takeaways as Trump's pick to lead the Fed faces a confirmation fight
rows.standfirst: President Trump's pick to lead the Federal Reserve went before a Senate committee today — but Kevin Warsh's confirmation could be held up by forces that are outside his control.

rows.title: She raised concerns about her company's contracts with ICE. Then she lost her job
rows.standfirst: Billie Little had worked for Thomson Reuters for about two decades. She was fired after questioning whether federal immigration agents unlawfully used their products.

rows.title: Corporate landlords aren't the real villain
rows.standfirst: So you want to buy a house. You MIGHT notice that the owner isn’t a neighbor in your town, but a large corporation. A recent housing bill that passed the Senate wants to change that. This bill would restrict large institutional investors from owning too many single family homes. The hope is to improve affordability. But what’s the real connection between housing affordability and corporate landlords? We look at the evidence.

rows.title: The Onion has agreed to a new deal to take over Infowars
rows.standfirst: The Onion says it has a new deal to take over conspiracy theorist Alex Jones' Infowars media company. If approved, the satirical news website could turn Infowars into a parody of itself.

rows.title: Trump's labor secretary resigns amid investigation into misconduct
rows.standfirst: Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer, who was under internal investigation, is leaving her position. She becomes the third cabinet departure of President Trump's second term.

rows.title: Is anyone gonna do anything about these Iran War trades?
rows.standfirst: Traders have made millions betting on the Iran War. They are also suspiciously timed. No public information, then boom: a Truth Social post from President Trump. Cue fat windfalls for the traders. It’s starting to look a lot like insider trading.

rows.title: Businesses race to apply for tariff refunds
rows.standfirst: Exactly two months after the Supreme Court struck down most of President Trump's tariffs, businesses that paid those levies began requesting refunds Monday.

rows.title: Photos: How overfishing in Southeast Asia is an ecological and human crisis
rows.standfirst: A rare look at one of the world's most critical and understudied environmental crises. Southeast Asia produces more than half of the world's fish, yet its waters are among the most depleted and contested.

rows.title: Tired of waiting for your EV to charge up? One Chinese company has a novel solution
rows.standfirst: Chinese car company NIO is putting up EV battery swapping stations all around the world. NPR took a ride in one car for the experience.

rows.title: Judge halts local TV giant Nexstar's takeover of rival Tegna until trial
rows.standfirst: U.S. Judge Trevor Nunley ruled that consumers could suffer irreparable harm if Nexstar integrated Tegna's stations into its own operations ahead of an antitrust trial.

rows.title: Do prediction market bettors make anything better?
rows.standfirst: Have you noticed a lot of young people getting into antenna-maxxing as alpha? Or, maybe searching for any bit of copium after they fat-fingered and got rinsed? Or maybe they farmed during a yes-fest on Mention Markets resulting in some serious printing?

rows.title: Gasoline could drop below $4 in coming days
rows.standfirst: Gasoline costs should start to fall soon, although a full recovery to pre-war prices is expected to take months. That's assuming that peace holds and traffic flows resume through the Strait of Hormuz.

rows.title: Fed chair, health care, and AI shoe repair
rows.standfirst: It’s Indicators of the Week. Our weekly look at some of the most fascinating economic numbers from the news.

rows.title: NPR receives $113 million in charitable gifts
rows.standfirst: "My hope is that this commitment provides the stability and the spark NPR needs to innovate boldly and strengthen its national network," says Connie Ballmer, who gave $80 million of the $113 million.

rows.title: Trump gives the go-ahead for a major new Canada-U.S. oil pipeline
rows.standfirst: More state and federal approvals are needed for the 3-foot-wide Bridger Pipeline Expansion, which would stretch from the Canadian border with Montana down through eastern Montana and Wyoming, where it would link up with another pipeline.

rows.title: The Onion's bid to take over Infowars moves to the Texas Supreme Court
rows.standfirst: The state's highest court will now consider a deal that would allow the Onion to license the Infowars brand name and turn the show into a mockery of itself.

rows.title: These fans are boycotting the World Cup. Will they make it a bust?
rows.standfirst: Some fans in the U.S. and around the world are unhappy with World Cup ticket prices — and U.S. immigration policies. So they're deciding not to come, raising concerns across the travel industry.

rows.title: The U.S. economy shows resilience despite the war with Iran
rows.standfirst: The U.S. economy revved up in the first three months of the year, despite a spike in energy prices caused by the war with Iran.

rows.title: The UAE wants a dollar lifeline
rows.standfirst: With the Iran War underway, the United Arab Emirates is looking for some economic certainty. The rich Arab nation is home to a lot of foreign-held deposits, and they’re worried investors will pull those funds. So, they’re looking for an economic backstop. Enter: currency swap lines. Today, we explain why the UAE is looking to its close ally, the U.S., for a currency swap line and how it would work.

rows.title: What Spirit Airlines’ rise and fall tells us about the future of cheap flights
rows.standfirst: It’s way more than fuel costs that pushed Spirit Airlines to the brink of liquidation and led President Trump to muse about “buying” them. Many low cost airlines are struggling due to a canny and calculated set of strategies from bigger airlines that we can think of as ‘revenge of the legacy carriers.’

rows.title: Elon Musk accuses OpenAI's leaders of 'looting the nonprofit' in court testimony
rows.standfirst: In his second day on the stand in the trial he launched against OpenAI, Elon Musk said the AI start-up he'd helped found had strayed from its charitable mission.

rows.title: At 82, she's jumping into the fight over immigration. Here's why
rows.standfirst: As the Supreme Court weighs the Trump administration's termination of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Syrians, seniors are advocating for protections for their immigrant caregivers.

rows.title: Spirit Airlines tried to be the Dollar General of the skies. Then the big airlines beat it at its own game
rows.standfirst: Spirit Airlines helped pioneer ultra-cheap flying and soared. Then legacy airlines copied them, outmaneuvered them with loyalty programs, and the economy turned against their core customers.

rows.title: Jerome Powell to remain on Fed's board after stepping down as chair
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve voted to hold interest rates steady, at what's likely Jerome Powell's last meeting as Fed chair. Kevin Warsh looks set to replace Powell next month.

rows.title: Why Sen. Warren voted no for Kevin Warsh as Fed chairman
rows.standfirst: Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren discusses the future of the Federal Reserve and tells NPR's Steve Inskeep why she plans to vote no on Kevin Warsh's nomination as Fed chair.

rows.title: The new economic arms race
rows.standfirst: Iran’s weaponization of the Strait of Hormuz is the perfect example of how modern warfare is increasingly waged, not only with drones and bombs, but also through the weaponization of economic choke points.

rows.title: FCC orders early license renewal for ABC stations following Kimmel's first lady joke
rows.standfirst: The Federal Communications Commission has ordered Disney's ABC to seek early broadcast license renewals for the eight TV stations it owns amid backlash over Jimmy Kimmel's joke about Melania Trump.

rows.title: Elon Musk testifies against OpenAI, seeking Sam Altman's ouster
rows.standfirst: Musk's lawyers say OpenAI leaders "stole a charity" and Musk warns about the potential dangers of AI: "We don't want to have a Terminator outcome."

rows.title: The United Arab Emirates is quitting OPEC oil cartel after nearly 60 years
rows.standfirst: The Arab oil producer has long expressed frustration with the quotas it has to follow as part of OPEC, the cartel of major state-owned oil producers.
